evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Adds gravity as accumulating velocity, bounce damping (restitution) and dt-correct friction, with an explicit units section separating position, velocity and acceleration.

Gravity is an acceleration: `skorost_y += G * dt` then `y += skorost_y * dt`, which is why falling starts slow and speeds up. -- Confirmed -- notebook 20-22 accumulates to 900.0 px/s after one simulated second at G = 900, and the generated gravity-fall-strip.png shows the growing gaps.

A restitution coefficient below 1 makes successive bounces lower; 1.0 is the lossless idealisation. -- Confirmed -- -900 * 0.8 = -720.0 in the notebook, and 300 px/s decays below 1 px/s in 26 bounces at 0.8, matching ln(300)/ln(1.25) = 25.6 -> 26.

Friction must be an acceleration applied through dt; multiplying velocity by a constant each frame makes braking frame-rate-dependent. -- Confirmed -- the reasoning is correct and is the same defect as 20.16's, correctly cross-referenced. The max()/min() clamps genuinely prevent overshooting through zero.
This is an arcade model, not a physics engine. -- Confirmed -- the callout correctly scopes what real engines add (rotation, mass, arbitrary shapes, many-body contacts).
